name: Travel trouble
desc: Lost passport, stolen phone or cards, medical care abroad, lost luggage, scams

s: Report it to the local police and get a written report (in Italy: Carabinieri or Polizia).
Contact your embassy or consulate: they can issue an emergency travel document.
Dutch citizens: the Dutch government's 24/7 contact centre (BZ) helps with this.
Bring a photo, the police report and a copy of the lost passport if you have one.
From another device: find, lock or erase it via Google Find My Device.
Block your SIM card with your mobile provider.
Change the passwords of your e-mail and banking.
Report it to the police for insurance.
Tell your group from someone else's phone.
Block your cards immediately in your bank app or by calling your bank (the number is on their website).
Check recent payments for anything you didn't do.
Report it to the police.
Use a backup card or cash; ask your bank about emergency cash.
Emergency: call 112 or go to the emergency department (Italy: “Pronto Soccorso”).
Not an emergency: a pharmacy (green cross) can advise; in Italy many tourist areas have a ‘guardia medica turistica’ in summer.
Show your European Health Insurance Card (on the back of a Dutch insurance card).
Call your own insurer's emergency line for big costs or hospital stays.
Report it at the airline desk before leaving the baggage hall and get the reference (PIR) number.
Keep receipts for essentials you have to buy.
Claim in writing in time: within 7 days for damage and 21 days for delayed bags.
Track the bag with the reference on the airline's website.
Only use official taxis or apps; agree the price or check the meter.
Be wary of ‘friendly’ helpers at ticket machines and ATMs.
Fake petitions, bracelets or ‘free’ gifts are often distractions for pickpockets.
Keep your phone and wallet in a front or zipped pocket in crowds.
